Not an expert but not sure why you would enter at 4 unless you got some nice PA. Easy in hindsight but that SZ at 1.9740, which is an FTR, looks far more significant and likely to get a reaction there.

Hi Mazdag,

The logic is based on the FTR articel, that if one breaks, you should look for a retrace before it moves down to the other side. One the flag limit at "1" had broken, according to the article, we should see a move to the bottom. As for the area at 1.9740, it looks like that has also tanked.

Yeah I understand what you're saying about "1" being engulfed, but I don't think that necessarily means that you short at the first area of supply that price comes to. "4" is an FTR but notice it has already had the FTB in the past, yours was 2TB so not going to be as strong - look for PA. The wider zone of the FTR at 40s is still holding but it may yet go higher to that area of supply you have marked up above 80s.
This is where clarification could go a long way. Do we trade the extreme of the most recent flag, which was the fail point in the image I posted, or is there a different approach?

"the extreme of the most recent flag"

Are you talking about point 4?
Yeah, that would be the coloured zone at "4."

There's no hard and fast rule as to where to short, as far as I'm aware. I think it just comes down to judgement, experience and personal preference. Some will take a TT, others will wait for PA - obviously waiting for PA would give you a little more certainty over the trade.

What I can say is I definitely wouldn't have taken a TT at 4 because it was 2TB. The area doesn't really stand out so I'm not even that bothered about looking for PA there. 40s looked a lot more attractive as an area of supply to me.
It would be handy if one approach could be drafted, as it seems as though everyone has a different way of reading the market.
